You're my opposite. For years now I've been counting steps, and I know that this is only anecdotal but I have found that most staircases are odd. This feeling is so strong such that I get mildly disappointed when I encounter an even flight of steps because it doesn't fit with my theory. I think that this even mitigates confirmation bias somewhat because I have a much stronger reaction to even-numbered stairs.

My step-counting began as a means to always land on the top step (I nearly always take steps two at a time). If I took one step, and then each successive step is double, assuming that the staircase has an odd number of steps, then my final step will reach the top without an awkward extra step. But it quickly became an obsession. I understand that it would be much more efficient to leave the offset step until the end and assume that all flights are even but it's just not the same!
Haha oh shit! The yin to my stair yang. Damn it's crazy you got so into it. Did it just kind of happen, you getting more obsessive about it haha?
